topic: Walter IOR-weighted rough refraction BTDF vs unweighted bisector rig
topic_zh: Walter 折射率加权微平面粗糙折射 BTDF 对比未加权平分线磨砂玻璃变黑
scope: Deterministic Bruce Walter et al. (EGSR 2007) IOR-weighted microfacet refraction half-vector (H_t = -normalize(eta_i*V + eta_o*L) with eta_i = 1.00, eta_o = 1.50, alpha = 0.25) versus naive unweighted bisector (-normalize(V + L)) and 64-step microfacet Snell root search across 17 incident viewing angles (theta_i in [0 deg, 80 deg]).

robustness.name: Sampled 17 incident viewing angles align the IOR-weighted half-vector with the Snell refraction lobe without off-axis darkening

good_fit: Frosted glass, etched crystal, ice cubes, and translucent polymers in glTF KHR_materials_transmission, Blender, and Three.js
Weighting incident and transmitted vectors by (eta_i, eta_o) so H_t = -normalize(eta_i*V + eta_o*L) satisfies Snell law
Eliminating the 12.37° half-vector tilt error and -68.06% at 60° / -83.64% at 80° transmission darkening of unweighted bisectors
Pairing with the Walter Refraction Jacobian eta_o^2*|L.H_t| / (eta_i*(V.H_t) + eta_o*(L.H_t))^2
not_for: Opaque metallic mirrors where reflection eta_i == eta_o makes the unweighted bisector exact
Zero-thickness flat decals without refraction IOR jump
Highly turbid multiple-scattering milk or skin (use Christensen-Burley BSSRDF Round 108)
